questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that were available were very important. Not all countries or universities have elaborate theologian studies or courses. But due to the nature of most universities in Korea, they all offer great and progressive programs in my field of study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The amount of work I had to do here, while also writing my final thesis was way too intense. I can not recommend that for anyone, instead I would go during a regular semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright. The school would send my emails about it, and there were different online forums that would keeo you updated on activities and so forth.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A big meeting were held within the first couple of days and there we were provided with all the information we needed. A handbook was also given to everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Every question was answered, and it was very clear that they a used to exchange students and the process of helping them in the beginning.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were two dorms specifically for exchange students.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a small tea kitchen on every floor and a larger kitchen in the basement of the big dorm. There were no meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's very convenient. If you plan a little bit, you can save a lot of money by cooking with some friends, but food is in general so cheap in Korea that it's not necessary. The rooms are by no means clean when you move in, so buy some sanitizing spray and clean it. There is no bedsheets available, so bring your own. Don't get in the way of the cleaning ladies, they are fierce and should not be provoked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I made some lifetime friends there and that's what really mattered to me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The description on how to do it sounded so confusing, but when you did it it was actually really simple.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get a certain amount of points and then you divide those points between the courses you want. The more points, the higher your chance of getting it. That's the first round. Then you will either have gotten the courses you want or not. The second round you can then either drop the courses you don't want, or look for new courses that are available if you didn't get the courses you wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They offered to help you register many times and also sent out a whole guidance powerpoint about the courses and how to register.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about the course registration. The teachers are easy to talk to, so you can always try to get your desired course by talking directly to the teacher.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Two of my courses were really interesting, the teacher were amazing and the level was adequate. The last course was absolutely horrible. The intention of the course was never clear and the teacher expressed racism, sexism and complete lack of knowledge in class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Like I said before, two of the courses were great, the last one was just unacademic and unprofessional.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is very similar, the teacher gives a lecture and based on the lecture you discuss different viewpoints.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to Psychology

Society and Human Behavior

Wisdom and the Art of Life

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intro to Psychology and Society and Human Behavior was great. A good introduction in the basics of both psychology and sociology. The teachers are really nice and engaging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Although I had a travel insurance from home, it was mandatory to pay the local health insurance as well, which was 71000 KRW every month. I did not expect that at all.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is inexpensive, clothes is inexpensive, coffee is cheap. Fresh fruit and vegetables is expensive and so is everything branded.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs. They were, as far as I know, not available to exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None. Exchange students were excluded from most activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go outside the campus, become friends with other exchange students, but also don't stay inside your exchange bubble. Try to explore Korea locally.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Seongsu is really nice area, Gangnam is overhyped, hike Ansan, it's in your backyard. Go to Sum, a local bar nearby. The owners are amazing and became our parents away from home.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. Just be respectful and be aware of your surroundings.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Socializing with local students is difficult because they take different courses than exchange students. So no, but learn as much Korean as you can from home.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There's a different culture when it comes to clothing. Not wearing a bra is considered sexual and wearing low cut necklines or showing your shoulders is also extremely sexualized. You don't have to conform to their views, but be aware that people will stare. Also, Korean people don't know how to walk on the street. It will make sense when you go.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The eating culture is great, also the silence is public transportation is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get out as much as possible, feeling alone is normal, it's expensive to be away from home.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't take Wisdom and the Art of Life.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having my friends, family and partner with me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would do it again. It was hard and amazing at the same time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
